extracted.intended_audience: policy makers, IP statisticians, patent office analysts, researchers and other users of WIPO patent statistics
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and data-definition notes for reading and comparing WIPO patent statistics (patent applications, PCT, PPH, patents in force, utility models, examiner data, gender attribution, etc.). Intended to help users correctly interpret metrics and cross-office comparisons.

rubrics_metrics.name: IPC-based technology definitions
rubrics_metrics.description: The correspondence between International Patent Classification (IPC) symbols and technology fields is not always apparent (there is no one-to-one correspondence). It is therefore difficult to capture all patents in a specific technology field.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: IPC-based definitions are likely to capture the vast majority of patent applications in these areas. For definitions of technologies (e.g., fuel cells, geothermal, solar, wind) see annex A. Users should be aware the mapping is imperfect and may omit some relevant patents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data refer to published patent applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Data presented (for technology charts, shares, etc.) refer to published patent applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Users should note the underlying counts are of published applications (not necessarily granted patents) when interpreting technology-specific figures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gender attribution to inventors' names
rubrics_metrics.description: In order to attribute gender to inventors’ names recorded in PCT applications, WIPO produced a world gender–name dictionary based on information from 13 different public sources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gender is attributed to a given name on a country-by-country basis, because certain names may be considered male in one country but female in another. Users should treat gender attribution as probabilistic and country-dependent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Share of applications granted — interpretation caution
rubrics_metrics.description: The share of applications granted should not be interpreted as grant rates, as they are based on the examination date rather than the date when the application was filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The number of grants in a given year relates to applications filed in previous years. Because of differences between offices’ procedures, data cannot be fully harmonized; exercise caution when comparing grant shares across offices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pending applications: category definitions
rubrics_metrics.description: To account for procedural differences, pending application data are separated between (a) all patent applications, at any stage in the process, that are awaiting a final decision by a patent office, including those for which applicants have not filed a request for examination (where applicable), and (b) patent applications undergoing examination for which the applicant has requested examination (where such separate requests are necessary).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some offices automatically proceed to examination; others require a request. Users must use the two-category separation to make meaningful comparisons across offices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Average age of patents in force — calculation
rubrics_metrics.description: The average age of patents in force is calculated using the following formula: ∑(p*y)/∑p, where p is the number of patents in force and y the number of years between filing and reporting year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the formula used for the reported average-age figures; users should apply the same formula if reproducing or comparing results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patents in force as percentage of total applications — calculation and interpretation
rubrics_metrics.description: Percentages are calculated as the number of patent applications filed in year t and in force in 2019, divided by the total number of patent applications filed in year t.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patent holders must pay maintenance fees to maintain validity; some patents lapse before the full term. Not all offices provide these data. The figure shows distribution of patents in force in 2019 by application year; do not assume completeness for offices that did not report.

rubrics_metrics.name: GDP data and top-20 origin inclusion criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: GDP data are in 2017 US purchasing power parity (PPP) dollars. The top 20 origins were included if they had a GDP greater than USD 25 billion PPP and more than 100 resident patent applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because of space constraints only the top 20 origins meeting these criteria are presented; users should be aware of selection criteria when interpreting per‑GDP metrics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resident patent applications per million population — inclusion criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: The top 20 origins were included if they had a population greater than 5 million and if they had more than 100 resident patent applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Due to space constraints only the top 20 origins fulfilling these criteria are presented; be cautious comparing to smaller jurisdictions excluded from the table.

rubrics_metrics.name: PCT counts — counting conventions
rubrics_metrics.description: Data refer to the international phase of the Patent Cooperation Treaty System. Counts are based on the international application date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For maps and origin breakdowns, counts are based on the residency of the first named applicant and the international application date. Use these conventions when reproducing PCT counts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent Prosecution Highway (PPH) — definition
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent prosecution highway is a bilateral agreement between two offices that enables applicants to request a fast-track examination whereby patent examiners can use the work already undertaken by the other office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Graphs and tables showing PPH flows use this definition; starred notes indicate instances where data are based on office of earlier examination rather than office of first filing.

rubrics_metrics.name: PPH data caveat (office-specific notes)
rubrics_metrics.description: * indicates data based on office of earlier examination rather than office of first filing (example: Japan).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Users should account for starred data differences when interpreting flows between offices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Microorganism deposits — patent procedural requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Deposits of microorganisms for patent procedures are important for biotechnological inventions. Disclosing an invention is a requirement for receiving a patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The number of deposits is reported because many biotech patents rely on microorganism deposits; users should be aware of deposit practices when assessing biotech patenting activity.

rubrics_metrics.name: World totals and office coverage notes
rubrics_metrics.description: World totals are WIPO estimates using data covering N offices (e.g., 127 offices for some series, 80 offices for utility model totals).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coverage varies by series; users should check the stated coverage for each table/figure. Example: utility model world totals include data covering 80 offices; world totals are estimates derived from that coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: China data comparability caveat
rubrics_metrics.description: China’s pre-2017 data are not comparable due to a change in methodology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because of this break in the data series and China’s large filing volume, world-level growth rates (e.g., 2017) may not be accurately reported; treat trends involving China with caution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data collection and harmonization caveat
rubrics_metrics.description: WIPO collects data from IP offices using a common questionnaire and methodology. However, due to differences in patent procedures between offices, data cannot be fully harmonized.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercise caution when making direct comparisons across offices; procedural and reporting differences can materially affect measures such as grant shares, pendency, and pending application counts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Average pendency times — interpretation caveat
rubrics_metrics.description: WIPO reports average pendency times for first office action and final decision at selected offices, but differences in patent procedures between offices make direct harmonization difficult.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use caution when comparing pendency across offices; institutional and procedural differences (e.g., request-for-examination regimes) affect measured pendency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equivalent applications by origin — completeness caveat
rubrics_metrics.description: Equivalent applications by origin data are incomplete because some offices do not report by origin.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tables labelled 'equivalent applications by origin' may undercount origins; users should not assume full global coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resident applications not reported — implication
rubrics_metrics.description: Some offices did not report resident applications; therefore equivalent applications by origin data may be incomplete.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where resident filing counts are missing, origin-based aggregates can be biased; check per-office footnotes (a–g) indicating reporting gaps or special cases.
